summary.text: 票 is written today with 覀 over 示. Its older written form 𤐫 is glossed “fire flying”; later uses include light movement and rapidity, and separate document and ticket senses. The evidence does not establish a direct development from fire to documents or tickets.

formation.text: 票 is a derived graph from the older form 𤐫, analyzed as an upper graphic element plus 火 and glossed “fire flying” or “fire rising.” In clerical writing, the upper part was reduced to 覀 and the lower 火 was written 示. The upper element is not securely identified as an object or action; the evidence does not establish a sparks scene or an altar-and-offering interpretation.

components.text: In historical graph 𤐫, the lower 火 is identified as its fire element, matching the gloss “fire flying/rising.” It was later written 示 through clerical change.
The upper element of historical graph 𤐫 is transcribed as 𦥑囟. Its depicted referent or action is not securely identified, and no sound role is established.

history.text: The older graph 𤐫 is described as a predecessor of 票. Its upper element was reduced to 覀, while lower 火 was written 示 in the clerical form behind modern 票. The documented inventory includes seal-script and bamboo-slip examples, but no oracle-bone or bronze examples; that does not establish whether earlier forms existed.
The proposed paired-hands, basket, sparks, and altar interpretations go beyond the supported identification of the older graph’s upper element and its fire gloss.

uncertainties.text: The upper element of 𤐫 is not securely identified, and the cited analyses do not establish a phonetic component in 票.
The selected historical glyph set contains no images, so the visible details of 𤐫 cannot be checked here against an image.

senses.period: dating unresolved; gloss reported in Shuowen
senses.text: The older graph 𤐫 is associated with the gloss “fire flying” or “fire rising.” This does not establish that the gloss was the earliest attested use or the graph’s original meaning.

senses.period: Qin and Han examples reported; earliest priority unresolved
senses.text: Older examples record light movement and shaking. A Qin-slip use 票風 is interpreted as a strong or rapid wind, but the evidence does not demonstrate a dated transition from the fire gloss.

senses.period: Qin and Han examples reported; earliest priority unresolved
senses.text: The character occurs in expressions associated with rapid movement, including the reported Qin-slip 票風 and Han shu examples. A separate Shuihudi phrase, 票行, has disputed readings and is not secure support for this sense.

senses.gloss: written or printed credential; ticket or ballot
senses.period: Ming-era and later examples; earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: 票 is used for documentary credentials and in modern compounds such as 車票, 門票, and 選票. The examples do not establish its first use or a direct development from the fire or motion senses.

senses.period: Qing-era and later examples; earliest attestation unresolved
senses.text: Paper-money uses are recorded in Qing-era and later examples. Their relationship to the fire, motion, or credential senses is not established.
This meaning is recorded in the supplied definition, without a dated example establishing its chronology or relation to the credential and ticket senses.

developments.text: Dictionary accounts associate the fire gloss with later light movement, but do not establish a continuous, dated transition.

limitations.text: The listed senses do not establish a complete sequence. The Qin-slip 票風 reading is reported in a scholarly dictionary; the separate reading of 票行 is disputed.
No direct semantic bridge is established from fire or rapid motion to credentials, tickets, ballots, or paper money.

overview.text: 票 is used today for tickets, slips, and documents. Its older written form was glossed “fire flying,” though the later ticket and document meanings are not shown to come from that sense.

components.text: The older form includes 火, the fire element in the gloss “fire flying.” In the later graph, this part was written 示.
The older form also has an upper element, but its depicted referent is not securely identified.

relationships.text: 𤐫 is identified as an older written form of 票. Its upper element was reduced, and its lower 火 was changed to 示 in clerical writing.
In the historical graph 𤐫, lower 火 is identified as the fire element in the gloss “fire flying/rising.”
